industry.ipm: The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) is worth over US$27 bn and grew ~8% in FY26 (AR FY26); growth picked up to ~12% in the Jun-2026 quarter (AIOCD Pharmatrac: volume 2.0%, price 5.8%, new products 3.3%). Chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, CNS, gastro) are ~56% of the IPM and grow faster than acute; they are 75% of Torrent's India sales.
themes: Cardiac, diabetes and CNS grow 10-13% a year; Torrent + JB is #1 in cardiac, #3 in CNS and gastro.
Larger companies keep adding reps and brands; Torrent grew 15% in FY26 and 19% in Q1FY27 vs the IPM's 9-12%.
First-to-market launches add growth (Torrent: ₹50 cr of semaglutide in Q1FY27), but prices fall fast as rivals enter (oral price cut from ₹149 to ₹109 a tablet).
Annual price increases on scheduled drugs are capped at WPI; cheaper trade generics and Jan Aushadhi compete in mass markets.
Large deals (JB-Torrent; earlier Curatio, Unichem) move share to scale players that can re-deploy brands through bigger field forces.
Price erosion of ~5-6% a year (AR FY26); tariffs exempted generics so far; Torrent's US sales are back to their FY14 level in dollars.
Insurer tenders award volumes to the cheapest bidder; annual price cuts; supply failures cost share.
Market ~BRL 249 bn growing ~11%; branded generics and generics both growing; ANVISA approval delays are the bottleneck.

moat: Brands and doctor reach (India)
Strong
27 mother brands above ₹100 cr; #1 in cardiac, #3 CNS and gastro; 75% chronic; ~9,000 reps after the JB merger; PCPM ~₹10 lakh.
Prescription habits are sticky; scale lets Torrent push acquired brands harder.
Acquisition integration
Strong (proven)
Elder (2014), Unichem (2017) and Curatio (2022) all grew faster under Torrent; Curatio +27-34% a year.
The JB case rests on repeating this; the record is the best evidence that it can.
Brazil franchise
Moderate
#1 Indian company in Brazil; outgrows the market (Q1FY27 +19% vs +4%, IQVIA); 58 products pending at ANVISA.
Durable but small (10% of FY26 revenue) and currency-exposed.
Cost position in generics (US, Germany)
Weak
US sales flat in dollars for a decade; Germany loses tenders to cheaper bidders; a key supplier failed.
No moat: these businesses are price takers.
Regulatory and quality
Adequate
All four US-supplying plants cleared by the USFDA; past Indrad/Dahej problems resolved.
Removes a discount, adds no premium.
CDMO (JB lozenges)
Moderate
JB's CDMO grew 27% in Q1FY27; sticky multinational customers.
Small (~₹700 cr of contract manufacturing revenue in FY26 incl. Torrent's own).
critiques: The JB price was full: ~₹25,700 cr for a business with ₹1,107 cr of FY26 EBITDA (23x), funded with ₹12,500 cr of debt. Returns on capital fall from 27% (FY25 ROCE) to the mid-teens until synergies arrive.
Reported EPS is depressed for 15 years by ~₹1,340 cr a year of brand amortisation; P/E comparisons with history must adjust for it (we do).
Brand transfers from JB to Torrent divisions in Q2-Q3 FY27 can lose prescribers; management itself expects 'some transition impact'.
Germany is 'in the middle of the woods': supplier failure and lost tenders; US sales are no higher in dollars than in FY14.
Semaglutide: first-mover share in India is being eroded by price cuts and new entrants; Brazil approval lost to five rivals.
The stock already trades at ~58x our FY28E reported EPS; MOSL and ICICI Securities see limited upside.
A ₹5,000 cr QIP enabling resolution was passed at the Jun-2026 AGM: an equity raise would dilute holders by ~3%.
gaps: Company press releases and investor presentations (torrentpharma.com HTML pages return 403 to automated access; PDFs of transcripts were readable); quarterly geography taken from PL tables.

Methods and estimates of ICICI Securities (Hold ₹4,925) and Geojit (Hold ₹4,898) are not public; Nomura, Kotak, Jefferies, Nuvama notes dated Jun-Sep 2026 were not found (marketscreener blocks automated access).
MOSL's 31-Jul-2026 EPS estimates are not public; we use its 23-May-2026 FY27E/FY28E EPS (₹66/₹92), which it said it 'largely maintained'.
JB's India vs international split for FY26 is not disclosed; we use the Q1FY27 split (61/39).
Named institutional holders (above 1%) for Jun-2026 were not retrieved; only categories and the promoter vehicle.
The ₹1,340 cr annual JB amortisation is the Q4FY26 stub run-rate (₹257 cr in 70 days) confirmed by the CFO; the split between brands, customer relationships and licences by year is not disclosed.
Q1FY27 split of other income between treasury income and FX/hedging loss is not disclosed.
conflicts: Q1FY27 EPS: Screener shows ₹16.72 (profit over 33.84 cr shares); the company reported ₹14.87 (post-merger share count). We use ₹14.87.
Q4FY26 profit: Screener shows ₹364 cr (before the -₹25 cr minority share) and EPS ₹10.76; profit to owners was ₹389 cr (FY26 ₹2,163 cr less Q1-Q3), EPS ₹11.51.
PL's note says net debt is '~INR 223bn'; on the company's 2.07x net debt/EBITDA and Mar-26 balance sheet it is ~₹12,700 cr (₹127 bn). We use the balance sheet.
Revenue by geography: the AR's segment note allocates by customer location (India ₹8,161 cr in FY26) while the MD&A/press release shows India business ₹7,645 cr; we use the MD&A split throughout.
Germany FY26: ₹1,249 cr in the revenue table vs ₹1,243 cr in the MD&A text (EUR 121 mn).
